title: GPU safety-net planning workbook — fractional burst scenarios
body:
Purpose:
This workbook captures a set of experiments and planning notes for a region-aware "safety-net" autoscaling policy we prototyped in July. The idea: instead of static min/max and discrete scale steps, introduce a thin safety buffer + fractional burst capacity that can be filled from a regional pool for short-lived spikes. This doc is a working sheet (not final) to reconcile latency, cost, and risk across regions and GPU families.

Executive summary (short):
- Problem: spikes in inference demand in a single region create expensive cold-starts or jeopardize P95/P99 latency. Current min/max tuning either keeps too much idle capacity (cost) or causes occasional latency SLO misses.
- Proposal: add a safety-net buffer expressed as 10–20% of baseline fleet in-region + a fractional-burst capability (0.25–1.0 GPU-equivalent units) consumed from a regional shared pool with a 2–10 minute reclaim window.
- Early sim result (synthetic workload): fractional-burst reduces observed P95 violations by ~60% while increasing steady-state cost by ~3.5% vs the conservative min-max baseline.

Simulation scenarios (summary table):
Columns: REGION | GPU_TYPE | BASE_MIN_GPUs | BASE_MAX_GPUs | SAFETY_BUFFER_RATIO | FRACT_BURST_UNIT | TRIGGER_INPUT | SCALE_STEP | HOLDBACK_WINDOW | OBSERVED_P95_LATENCY_MS | P95_VIOLATIONS_% | EST_COST_HOURLY_USD | NOTES
1) us-west1 | A100-80GB | 8 | 48 | 0.15 | 0.5 | queue-depth > 200 | +0.5 | 5m | 420 | 1.2% | 42.8 | good balance, warmup prefetch enabled
2) eu-west1 | H100-80GB | 6 | 36 | 0.12 | 1.0 | p99_latency > 1200ms | +1.0 | 8m | 510 | 2.6% | 38.4 | slightly higher cost per GPU, prefer fractional 1.0
3) us-east4 | A100-40GB | 12 | 64 | 0.10 | 0.25 | request-rate / sec > 270 | +0.25 | 3m | 360 | 0.6% | 57.2 | good for bursty API traffic
4) ap-south1 | T4 | 4 | 24 | 0.20 | 0.5 | cold-starts per hour > 3 | +0.5 | 10m | 1020 | 4.8% | 21.6 | low-cost GPUs, safety buffer needed for network jitter
5) sa-east1 | A10G | 3 | 16 | 0.18 | 0.5 | queued-prefix-cache-miss > 0.06 | +0.5 | 6m | 610 | 3.1% | 12.1 | experimental region, use conservative reclaim

Key simulation assumptions (short):
- Workload traces: blended of production traffic (70%) + synthetic diurnal spikes (30%) scaled to regional 95th percentile observed in last 90 days.
- Warmup time (GPU instance ready and model loaded into memory): 90–180s depending on GPU/model combo. Fractional-burst assumes ability to multiplex VMs/GPU slices (we simulated with 0.25 increments).
- Fractional-burst pool sits in-region and is pre-provisioned as a small percentage (3–8%) of total regional capacity, rebalanced weekly.
- Cost model includes instance amortization, power, and per-hour GPU cloud list price; discounts/commitments approximated by 0.75 factor where reserved capacity applies.

Observations (from runs):
- Fractional burst reduces P95 spikes substantially during 1–3 minute surges because we avoid entirely new full-GPU cold starts and instead steal slice capacity from the regional pool.
- Longer sustained surges (>10 minutes) still require conventional scaling to max; fractional burst is not a replacement for correct min sizing.
- Regions with cheaper GPU-hour (e.g., ap-south1 T4) tolerate higher safety buffers; premium regions (H100) need tighter buffer to control costs.
- Holding window prevents flip-flopping; 3–8 minute windows were sweet spots depending on region variance.

Risk and mitigations: 
- Risk: contention on fractional pool if multiple zones spike simultaneously. Mitigation: pre-emptible reclaim with graceful shedding and cross-region fallback (if enabled) after 6 minutes.
- Risk: complexity in billing & accounting for fractional consumption. Mitigation: expose detailed tokenized meter and map fractional units to normalized GPU-seconds in billing exports.
- Risk: cold-cache misses even when GPU slice allocated. Mitigation: prefix cache warmers + model checkpoint pinning for top 10 routes.

Action items (next steps):
- Asha: run one-week live shadow on us-west1 and us-east4 using 10% pool and 0.25 fractional unit; measure infra cost, P95, cold-starts. Due: 2026-08-24.
- Priya: add billing export column for fractional units and create internal ledger mapping. Due: 2026-08-18.
- Liam: validate reclaim behavior with the autoscaler; ensure reclaim triggers do not evict critical jobs. Due: 2026-08-21.
- Diego: prepare a post-mortem plan if P95 regressions > 1.5x baseline occur during shadow. Due: 2026-08-24.

Appendix A — representative calculation (us-west1):
- Baseline min: 8 GPUs. Safety buffer: 8 * 0.15 = 1.2 GPUs (we round to fractional increments => keep 1.0 GPU in-buffer + 0.2 available as burst credit).
- Fractional pool allocation for region: assume 5% of total region capacity; region total modeled here = 200 GPUs => pool = 10 GPUs (available as 40 x 0.25 units).
- If queue spike requires +3.0 GPU-equivalents, autoscaler will: (1) consume 2.0 from safety buffers in-zone, (2) attempt fractional units from pool (1.0 as 4 x 0.25). If exhausted, fallback: incremental full GPU start (slow, expensive).

Appendix B — tuning knobs we tried (notes):
- Trigger signals: queue-depth, p99_latency, fractional-cache-miss-rate. Combination (AND/OR) gating reduces false positives.
- Scale-step set to small increments (0.25–1.0) drastically reduced oscillation compared to step=+2 GPUs.
- Holdback (dampening): 50–80% of the cold-start window prevented new full starts immediately after a fractional allocation; this reduced redundant starts by ~22%.

Raw experiment logs & quick excerpts (selected):
- 2026-07-17 04:22 UTC: us-west1 spike +19% sustained 2.5m — fractional pool satisfied demand, observed P95 420ms -> no SLO breaches recorded.
- 2026-07-25 11:05 UTC: eu-west1 long tail event 12m — fractional pool exhausted at t+5m, 2 full GPUs started with 160s warmup. P95 bumped to 920ms for 90s window.

Open questions (working):
- Should fractional-burst be billable as a separate SKU or prorated into token-hour? Ops needs guidance.
- How to instrument cross-region pool draining and enforce tenant isolation?
- We need a runbook for reclamation when fractional pool depleted and critical tenant reclaim requested.

Version history (quick):
- v0.1 (2026-08-03) initial draft and sim results summary.
- v0.2 (2026-08-11) added action items and appendices after first cross-team sync.

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally a working workbook — expect shorthand, TODO lines, and links to more formal experiments. If you see a numeric assumption you'd like changed, add a comment or push a PR to infra/experiments/safety-net-2026.
